children: GIFT City's International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) has emerged as a major hub for foreign currency mobilisation, with IFSC Banking Units (IBUs) sanctioning over $54 billion under the Reserve Bank of India's special swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, of which around $52.8 billion has been disbursed, the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) said.

As of August 31, 2026, 20 IBUs had sanctioned $54.02 billion under the facility. Sanctions rose sharply through August, from $28.6 billion on August 14 to $37.26 billion on August 21, and further to $54.02 billion by month-end. Participating IBUs include both leading Indian and foreign banks operating out of GIFT-IFSC.

The IFSCA said the scale of activity reflects GIFT-IFSC's ability to connect banking units with global pools of foreign currency liquidity and channel that capital into India. The development follows a directive from the Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman to MDs and CEOs of public sector banks to make greater use of GIFT-IFSC's infrastructure for implementing the RBI's swap facilities for FCNR(B) deposits and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs).

Beyond the FCNR(B) window, IBUs disbursed $11.62 billion in ECBs between April and August 2026, with monthly disbursements rising from $1.54 billion in April to $3.54 billion in August. Indian banks also raised $11.12 billion through bond listings on IFSC exchanges over the same period, including $9.17 billion in July-August alone.
Funds were mobilised from multiple jurisdictions, including the UK, US, Mexico, West Asia, Hong Kong, Singapore and parts of Africa, the authority said.

IFSCA Chairperson K. Rajaraman said, "The rapid scale-up of banking activity at GIFT-IFSC is a strong testament to the depth, capability and growing international orientation of India's GIFT City International Financial Services Centre. The mobilisation and deployment of over $52 billion under the FCNR(B) swap facility, alongside strong ECB activity by IBUs in GIFT IFSC and international bond listings at IFSC Exchanges, demonstrate that GIFT-IFSC is increasingly serving as an effective bridge between global pools of capital and India's financing needs."
He added that the IFSCA remains committed to a competitive, well-regulated and globally connected financial ecosystem at the centre.

title: GIFT City IFSC mobilises over $52.8 billion under RBI's FCNR(B) swap facility
